holidays.name: National Cat Day
holidays.description: A day to shower your favorite felines with treats, cuddles and extra toys, and to spotlight shelter cats who need homes. Expect a lot of purring and a lot of photos.
holidays.origin: Pet and family lifestyle expert Colleen Paige created National Cat Day in 2005 to encourage cat adoption and to remind people how many cats need homes.
holidays.funFact: Cats sleep roughly 12 to 16 hours a day, so for most cats every day is already a day of rest.

holidays.name: International Internet Day
holidays.description: A salute to the web that lets you read about weird holidays, watch cat videos and argue about oatmeal. It's a good day to remember how much of daily life now runs online.
holidays.origin: The date points back to October 29, 1969. On that day, researchers sent the first message between two computers on the ARPANET, the precursor to the modern internet. The message was meant to be the word LOGIN.
holidays.funFact: The system crashed after the first two letters, so the very first message sent over the ARPANET was 'LO', as in 'lo and behold.'

holidays.name: National Hermit Day
holidays.description: A day for people who love peace and quiet. Cancel the plans, silence the phone and enjoy a little solitude with a good book, a cup of tea or a hobby of your choice.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with introverts and anyone who has ever wanted a day without small talk.
holidays.funFact: Hermit crabs are not true hermits. They often live in large social groups and will queue up to swap shells.
